resources.string: Start the 1-month free trial, then %1$s a month
Switch language on the keyboard: tap the language key (next to the comma).
How far a tap may miss a letter on the one-row keyboard and still count. Tight trusts your taps more; loose forgives bigger misses.
How closely the curve you draw across the full keyboard has to follow the letters of the word. Loose forgives a rough curve; tight trusts it more.
Loose – a rough curve is enough
A row of digits above the letters. Hold a digit for superscripts and fractions (³, ½, ⅓, ¼ ...).

Android underlines words in red using its own spell checker, which only knows one language. OneRow has its own: it knows every language you added here (and the words you taught it), so only really unknown words get marked.
Pick \"OneRow Keyboard\" on the screen that opens
Checking whether this phone can do it...

A check circle at the right end of the guess bar: tap it to fix the grammar and spelling of what you typed in the field, tap again to undo. English, French, German, Italian and Spanish. Runs on the phone; the first use may download a model.
Not available on this phone: it needs Google\'s on-device AI (Gemini Nano), which only some newer phones have.
Swipe typing on the full keyboard
Draw a word across the letters instead of tapping them. Swipe down on the guess bar to return to one row. The cheat sheet below shows every gesture.
Swipe left on the letter row: delete
Hold a letter, then slide: release types exactly that letter (no guessing)
Hold the period key, then slide to choose basic punctuation
Hold the comma key, then slide: the emoji you use most come first. Swipe up: all emoji (tap one)
Drag on space: move the cursor
Drag left on backspace: delete word by word
Swipe the guess bar sideways: more guesses
Hold a guess, drop it on the bin: forget the word
Tap the language key: next language
Hold the language key, then slide: settings, normal, floating, split (tablets only). Slide to the normal icon to dock a floating keyboard again
Floating keyboard: drag the handle on top to move it
Floating keyboard: drag the corner to resize it
Swipe typing (optional, Settings > Gestures): draw a word across the letters, here h-e-l-l-o. Tap a guess to replace the word; backspace deletes the whole word
Slide from 123 onto the keys: symbols and currency signs appear; release types one and goes back to the letters
Swipe down on the guess bar: back to one row. Pull up from the guess bar or the bottom row of the one-row keyboard: full keyboard
Shake the phone to see the crash report
A firm shake while the keyboard is open shows the last crash report. You can read it and email it to us. Nothing is sent unless you send the email yourself.

If the keyboard crashed, you can send us the technical details so we can fix it. The report below is everything that will be sent: the app and Android versions, the phone model, the language and the technical trace of the crash (which parts of the program were running). It contains nothing you typed, no clipboard, no contacts, no settings and no dictionary. Pressing Send only opens your email app with this text filled in; nothing leaves the phone until you send the email yourself.
No crash has been recorded on this phone, so there is nothing to send.
